cues: Cross pollination needs an agent, and each agent shapes the flower.
Wind flowers are small and dull, with masses of light pollen and feathery stigmas, like maize.
Water flowers, like Vallisneria, have pollen that will not get wet.
Insect flowers are bright, scented and full of nectar.
Bird flowers, like the red simal of the Terai, are large, red and tubular, with lots of nectar but no scent, because birds cannot smell well.
And bat flowers open at night and smell strongly.
